record.title: CARE reports improved recovery from robot failures using staged corrective demonstrations
record.summary: CARE trains robot policies to recover from failures drawn from their own execution patterns. It collects unsuccessful rollouts, models stage-conditioned deviations, synthesizes failure states and corrective demonstrations, and uses a staged planner with geometric monitoring before a unified vision-language-action executor. On FSR-Bench, the authors report improved recovery over comparison methods across five simulation tasks and four real dual-arm tasks. The real-robot evaluation uses a 12-DoF SO-101 platform and 100 trials per task; the paper reports a 15.9 percentage-point gain in its real-world comparison and a 7.5-point gain on the recovery-focused FSR measure. These are author-reported results in a single paper; the research desk did not independently reproduce them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On four real dual-arm tasks using a 12-DoF SO-101 platform, the authors report 100 trials per task and a 15.9 percentage-point gain in their overall comparison; their recovery-focused FSR measure improves by 7.5 points. These are results from the authors’ evaluation, not an independent reproduction.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On FSR-Bench, comprising 36 recovery scenarios across five tasks, the paper reports improved recovery, with train/test failure distributions separated. It also evaluates seven hard bimanual RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and three multi-arm RoboFactory tasks. The reported results are benchmark-specific and do not establish transfer to other platforms or failure distributions.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction was inspected. Real-robot evidence covers four tasks on one SO-101 platform; transfer to other embodiments and failure distributions is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, policy-native failure mining and staged correction could improve robot recovery without relying on arbitrary perturbations, an important weakness in long-horizon manipulation. The paper includes both simulation and real-robot trials, but one platform and author-run evaluation bound the consequence.
limitations: The quantitative findings are reported by the paper authors; no independent reproduction was inspected.
Real-robot evaluation covers four dual-arm tasks on one 12-DoF SO-101 platform with 100 trials per task; this does not establish cross-platform transfer.
FSR-Bench and the paper’s simulation suites are bounded benchmark regimes; performance on other failure distributions and deployment conditions remains unknown.

The reported gain depends on the full system, which combines failure mining, stage-conditioned correction, geometric monitoring and a staged planner; component-level attribution requires matched ablations.

brief.title: CARE reports improved recovery from robot failures using staged corrective demonstrations
brief.why_it_matters: Robots often fail after leaving the nominal demonstration path, while arbitrary perturbations may not resemble a policy’s actual failures. CARE reports gains from mining failures produced by the policy and training stage-specific corrections. If independently confirmed, this could shape how long-horizon robot recovery is trained and evaluated; current evidence is limited to the authors’ benchmark and one real-robot platform.
